text:
Oliver (PM): quick sync? reviewing latest model-catalog compare changes. main topics: badge density in rows, how pinning should feel (and surface), and whether filter choices follow you across pages.

Anya (Design): dropped a new set of frames in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc. Key ideas: 1) micro-badges, capped inline to 3 + overflow, 2) pin as a small action button on each row (always visible on focus), 3) a persistent pinned-items chip in the page header.

Ben (Eng): thumbs up on overflow cap. rendering 8 badges kills paint times. overflow should be a lightweight popover. concerning the pin: if we keep it visible on focus, we need clear keyboard target + hit area.

Dave (Accessibility): yes. must be keyboard reachable and announceable. suggest: native button element, aria-label="Keep this version in compare", aria-pressed toggles state. also ensure the overflow button reports aria-expanded.

Carla (Product): one product constraint: customers want pins to be shareable (so a link reproduces the pinned set). idea: encode pins in query like `?pinned=model:1234@v2.1` and support multiple pinned params.

Ben (Eng): encoding multiple pins in the URL is fine but can get long. we should support a compact form: `?pins=md1234:v2.1,md9876:v1.0` and fallback to localStorage aliasing for very long lists. backend doesn't need to persist it.

Anya (Design): microcopy question: pin button tooltip text. current brainstorm: "Keep in compare" vs "Pin for compare" vs "Save this version to compare". shorter copy preferred.

Carla (Product): prefer "Keep in compare" — reads clearer in the context of the compare view. also add a subtle info toast when pin is added: "Version kept for compare. Shareable link updated."

Ben (Eng): note: to avoid overusing toasts, the URL update should be silent; only show toast if user clicks "Copy share link" or when a pin action fails.

Dave (Accessibility): if we update URL silently we need an aria-live region that announces the change for screen-reader users: "Added version v2.1 to compare". also ensure focus isn't stolen by the toast.

Anya (Design): badges: plan is 3 inline badges + "+n" pill. clicking +n opens a keyboard-traversable list with full names and descriptions. for performance badges (latency/cost) we propose a single compact metric badge (p95) visible inline; other metrics land in the overflow.

Carla (Product): on metrics: ops asked to surface both latency and cost. designers worry about clutter. compromise: primary metric toggle — default to p95 latency, optional cost column user can enable from the table settings.

Ben (Eng): feature flag idea: add per-workspace table preferences stored in localStorage and a short endpoint to optionally persist to account settings later. implementing the column toggle now can be kept client-side.

Dave (Accessibility): for the metric sparkline in the hover popover: include a text fallback in the popover header like "p95 latency (median 120ms, latest 112ms)" so screen readers get the numbers.

Anya (Design): mobile: no hover, so pin and overflow go into row action menu (three dots). pinch tap to open actions.

Carla (Product): deprecated/pinned conflict: what if a pinned version is deleted or gated? we should show a placeholder row with explanation and CTA "Pick replacement". also mark deprecated versions with a dimmed badge "deprecated" so users notice.

Ben (Eng): implementation plan: on load, resolve pinned params -> verify existence via metadata endpoint -> if missing, fetch nearest compatible version or mark missing and surface replacement flow. keep compare layout stable in all cases.

Dave (Accessibility): quick checklist I'll add to the spec doc: keyboard targets for pin and overflow, aria-pressed, aria-expanded, aria-live for state changes, color contrast for badges (>=4.5), and focus styling for the pinned chip in header.

Anya (Design): microcopy for metric tooltip: "p95 latency — calculated from recent production traffic. Click for detailed trend." ok?

Carla (Product): yes. also add a short inline help link near the table header: "What do these badges mean?" opens a short modal with definitions.

Ben (Eng): dev note: avoid heavy SVGs per-badge; prefer CSS badges + a11y-friendly text. Also throttle fetches for sparklines to reduce backend load (debounce on hover).

DesignOps Bot: created ticket PROD-UX-432: Update model catalog table — badge overflow, pin UX, URL sync. Assignees: Anya, Ben. Due: 2026-04-07.

Anya (Design): I'll update the frames with keyboard flows and +n popover states by tomorrow.

Oliver (PM): great. Ben, can you spike URL param handling and local prefs this sprint?

Ben (Eng): yes, will put up a spike PR by Thu.

Carla (Product): thanks all. if anyone has copy tweaks for tooltips or modal text, drop them here or ping me. :sparkles:
